name: Feedback Studio
intro: This test opens Feedback Studio itself, not a test copy, because the purple test-copy bar covers its bottom buttons. You will open GameDay inside it, type a few comments (no talking needed), build the report, and send it to Jerry for real.

steps.do: Read the welcome card, then tap “Pick an app to review →”.
steps.see: The card closes. You see “Feedback Studio” and a list of quick picks grouped under YOUR HOUSEHOLD, LATER LIFE, YOUR CHURCH and more. At the bottom: a big red 🎙 button and “💬 Comments (0)”.
steps.tip: No welcome card? You have opened Feedback Studio before; just carry on. If it says “You have … comments from last time”, tap “🗑 Start fresh”.

steps.see: GameDay opens inside the window (its own welcome card may show — that is fine, leave it). At the top you see “‹ Start screen” and a small pill ending in “v1.4 · 2026-10-08”.

steps.do: Tap “💬 Comments (0)” at the bottom right.
steps.see: A “Session comments” panel opens: “No comments yet.”, a box that says “…or type a comment” with an “Add” button, and “✅ I’m done — build the report”. The button now reads “✕ Comments (0)”.
Nothing happens. Still “No comments yet.” and “Comments (0)”.

steps.do: Tap the “…or type a comment” box, type the example, then tap “Add”.
steps.type: The O'Brien kids' games are easy to find
steps.see: Your comment appears in the panel with a time like “0:05” next to it, apostrophes and all. The button now says “✕ Comments (1)”.

steps.do: Tap the gold “🚩 Mark” button at the bottom.
steps.see: A new comment appears: “🚩 MARKER — 🚩 Look at the screen right here — this spot matters.” The button says “✕ Comments (2)”, and the panel now shows “Show all 2”.

steps.do: Tap “Show all 2” at the top of the panel.
steps.see: Both comments are listed: your typed one and the 🚩 marker, each with its time and a small ✕.

steps.do: Pull the page down to reload it (or tap ↻ in Safari).
steps.see: Feedback Studio starts over at its start screen and asks “You have 2 comments from last time”, with “🗑 Start fresh” and “▶ Keep adding to them”.
The question closes and the bottom button still says “💬 Comments (2)”.

steps.do: Turn on Airplane Mode (swipe down from the top-right corner, tap ✈️). Tap “💬 Comments (2)”, type the example in the box, and tap “Add”.
steps.see: A brown strip at the top says “No connection right now — the app still works and saves on this phone.” Your new comment shows and the button says “✕ Comments (3)”.

steps.do: Turn Airplane Mode off. Then tap the green “✅ I’m done — build the report”.
steps.see: The brown strip goes away. A “Report for Claude” page opens with the written report; your three comments are in it. At the bottom: “📨 Send to Claude”, “Copy to clipboard” and other buttons.

steps.do: Scroll to the bottom of the report and tap “Copy to clipboard”. A box says “Report copied ✓” and asks whether to clear these 3 comments: tap Cancel (to keep them).
steps.see: The box closes. The report is still open with your comments in it.

steps.do: Tap “📨 Send to Claude”. If a box asks “Your first name, so Jerry knows who sent this:”, type your first name and tap OK.
steps.see: The report stays on the screen and nothing seems to change. (The thank-you note is hidden behind the report; the next step shows it.)
steps.tip: This really sends your test report to Jerry. That is what testers do, so it is fine.

steps.do: Tap “✕ Close” at the top right of the report. Then tap “✕ Comments (3)” at the bottom to close the comments panel.
steps.see: Just above the bottom buttons, a note says “✅ Sent. Thank you, (your name)! Jerry reads every report the same evening; fixes usually show up on your phone the next morning.” with a purple “Done” button.
The note closes. The bottom button still says “💬 Comments (3)”.

steps.do: Tap “💬 Comments (3)”, then tap “Clear” (next to the green “✅ I’m done” button). When asked “Clear all 3 comments and start fresh?”, tap OK.
steps.see: The panel says “No comments yet.” again and the button reads “✕ Comments (0)”.

steps.do: Tap “‹ Start screen” at the top left.
steps.see: GameDay closes and you are back on the Feedback Studio start screen with its quick picks, ready for the next app.
